posts.title: Top battery makers' share in China in July 2026: CATL 42.33%, BYD 19.23%
posts.summary:
CATL remained China's largest power battery maker in July, though its market share fell 0.37 percentage points from June.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: CATL maintained its lead in China's EV battery market in July with a 42.33% share, though it experienced a slight decline in both total installations and market percentage.
BYD continues to close the gap with CATL, increasing its market share by 0.74 percentage points to 19.23% during the same period.
The data highlights a competitive landscape where smaller players like Sunwoda and Rept Battero are gaining marginal share, while LG Energy Solution's domestic share has dropped to under 1%.

posts.title: BYD's third-gen Tang SUV to debut at Chengdu Auto Show on August 21
posts.summary:
BYD has officially named the previously teased 8-series Tang the third-generation Tang, a five-seat SUV with up to 850 km of range.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: BYD is set to debut the third-generation Tang SUV on August 21, a five-seat model designed to revitalize the flagship lineup following a sharp decline in sales for the current generation.
The new Tang features BYD's second-generation Blade Battery and flash charging technology, with variants offering up to 850 km of CLTC range.
The vehicle will come standard with the 'God's Eye B' driver-assistance system and DiSus-A intelligent body control, positioning it as a premium offering in the D-segment.

posts.title: Nvidia Backs OpenAI Data Center, Anthropic News, Google Buys Spirit Airlines Data
posts.summary: Nvidia makes another deal, this time with a frontier lab; Anthropic's revenue continues to amaze; and maybe data finally is oil.
bullets: Nvidia is deepening its strategic integration with the AI ecosystem by directly backing a new data center project for OpenAI.
Anthropic continues to demonstrate significant commercial momentum, with revenue growth figures that suggest a strong competitive position among frontier AI labs.
Google's acquisition of Spirit Airlines' data highlights a growing trend where non-tech companies are monetizing proprietary datasets as high-value assets for AI training.
The convergence of hardware investment, rapid revenue scaling in AI labs, and the commoditization of corporate data underscores the evolving 'data is oil' thesis in the current tech landscape.

posts.title: We still don’t know how people are really using AI
posts.summary: AI companies like Anthropic and OpenAI regularly publish reports on how people are using products like Claude and ChatGPT, but they only release the data they want us to see, AI researchers say.  “There is no independent source to corroborate it,” says Anka Reuel, a computer science PhD candidate at the Stanford Trustworthy AI Research…
bullets: The AI Observatory study reveals that nearly 48% of AI conversations are excluded from industry-standard productivity reports, which prioritize work-related use cases.

Independent analysis shows that non-work interactions frequently involve sensitive topics, including health, relationships, harassment, and sexual content, which are often omitted from corporate disclosures.
Current AI policy and risk assessments are being built on limited, curated datasets, creating a blind spot for researchers and regulators regarding the true societal impact of generative models.
The study suggests that relying solely on vendor-provided data, such as the Anthropic Economic Index, provides an incomplete picture of how consumers actually integrate AI into their daily lives.

posts.title: Blog Review: Aug. 19
posts.summary:
Memory tagging; digital twin of the Moon; packaging moves front-and-center; streaming sensor data.
The post Blog Review: Aug. 19 appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Advanced packaging has transitioned from a backend afterthought to a primary design discipline, with industry experts identifying the 'wire' as the defining challenge of modern chip architecture.
New methodologies for AI development are emerging, including physical AI frameworks that allow for the replay of real-world sensor data to validate algorithm improvements.
Energy efficiency is becoming a strategic imperative for all AI inference applications, extending the focus beyond data center builders to edge and system-level designers.
Industry leaders are prioritizing specialized hardware, such as fully programmable AI silicon and co-packaged optics, to address the rising power, latency, and thermal constraints of modern systems.
